items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Sister Jeanne, j-e-a-double n-e. She was the art teacher.

ctx.x: I was . . . the first . . . because now you know all the dates. In the first place, when I started . . . one of the things I remember was at the convent, because they had a very good, because they had a good art teacher, who was a nun. Of course they

mostly were nuns, although there were some regular teachers who were not nuns. Sister Jeanne, j-e-a-double n-e. She was the art teacher. It just consisted of her setting up something, an apple and a jug of water, the typical thing. “Draw this” or “Paint this.” And we did. I think most of these were taken from the next school, from Stratford House. Then we had another very good teacher, Miss Hollins. It was just a case of her setting up something and talking about perspective and all kinds of things they talk…
Like a logo type of thing.
